annotation.title_clean: The typification of infringement issues of humanoid robots: with special reference to the governance of infringement caused by learning algorithms
annotation.title_en: The typification of infringement issues of humanoid robots: with special reference to the governance of infringement caused by learning algorithms
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Department of Law, Shanxi University of Finance and Economics
annotation.summary_en: Chinese legal article classifying humanoid robot infringement into passive and active types, focusing on harm from learning algorithms. It proposes a law-and-economics allocation of liability among manufacturers (Hand Formula), users (reasonable care) and general AI model providers (joint liability for transparency failures).
key_provisions_or_claims: Humanoid robots' human-like appearance, intelligence and hybrid control create an anthropomorphic trap and expand infringement risk.
Infringement is typified into passive and active types; learning-algorithm failure is the most distinctive.
Manufacturers should follow dynamic national regulations guided by the Hand Formula.
Users are liable for negligent failure of reasonable care.
General AI model providers may be jointly liable with robot providers if they fail on transparency.
